outcome: No result found, in any source, that settles or narrows this specific question in the 26 January 2024 to present window.
summary: This bullet's own citation (visible on both the frozen January 2024 revision and the current live article, confirmed identical) is Saharon Shelah, 'Borel sets with large squares', Fundamenta Mathematicae 159 (1999), arXiv math/9802134. That 1999 paper is the origin of the question: it introduces the cardinal invariant λ_{ω1}(ℵ0) and proves (⊗'_μ) that if a complete sentence ψ of L_{ω1,ω} (equivalently, by Chang's trick, an atomic class of a countable first-order theory omitting countably many types) has a model of cardinality μ ≥ λ_{ω1}(ℵ0), then it has a model of cardinality continuum, generated in a 'nice, absolute' way — and shows this is consistent with λ_{ω1}(ℵ0) itself being at or above ℵ_{ω1} (e.g. under MA + 2^ℵ0 > ℵ_{ω1}), so the Hanf-number-below-continuum phenomenon at exactly ℵ_{ω1} is not settled by that theorem alone; whether ℵ_{ω1} always suffices, or whether it can consistently fail, is left open. The Wikipedia bullet is a restatement of this residual open case. I searched extensively for any post-26-January-2024 progress on this exact question: model theorists who work in the closest surrounding territory (John Baldwin, Chris Laskowski, Shelah himself, and collaborators) have been highly active in the general area of atomic classes / L_{ω1,ω} categoricity and Hanf-number-type questions through 2024-2025 — e.g. Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah, 'When does ℵ1-categoricity imply ω-stability?' (Model Theory 3 (2024) 801-823, arXiv 2308.13942, submitted Aug 2023 — before the window); Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah, 'An analogue of U-rank for atomic classes' (arXiv 2502.00984, Feb 2025); and Baldwin's two 2024 and 2025 conference talks 'Can categorical classes in L_{ω1,ω} be bounded in size?' (AEC Conference, Baylor, July 2024; Shelah's 80th birthday conference, Vienna, July 16 2025) — but I read the 2025 talk slides in full and none of this work touches the ℵ_{ω1}-to-continuum question; it is about a different (though related) pair of questions: whether ℵ1-categorical atomic classes/AECs have models bounded in size at all (Grossberg's question, the WGCH(λ) theorem, and the (2^ℵ0)+ implies ω-stability theorem), not about the Hanf number for omitting-types classes at ℵ_{ω1} specifically. I also checked the Kurepa-tree/L_{ω1,ω}-spectrum literature (Bagaria-Cummings-... adjacent work; Lambie-Hanson and Stejskalová's Nov 2024 'Kurepa trees, continuous images, and perfect set properties') and Shelah's 'On what I do not understand' problem list (1999/2000) — all pre-window or off-target. No arXiv listing, Baldwin publication page, or Shelah archive entry from 2024-2026 addresses this exact statement. There is no AI involvement anywhere in this literature; it is entirely human set-theoretic and model-theoretic work using forcing, weak diamond, and pseudo-algebraic-closure techniques.
competing_reading: The Baldwin-Laskowski-Shelah 2024/2025 line of work (ω-stability from a model of size (2^ℵ0)+, and the general 'can categorical classes in L_{ω1,ω} be bounded in size' program) is close enough in subject matter that a very loose reading might count it as 'progress adjacent to this problem.' I judge it does not count under §3.1: it answers a different question (boundedness of ℵ1-categorical atomic classes, and ω-stability transfer) rather than moving the specific ℵ_{ω1}→continuum implication for theories omitting countably many types. It is a related problem, not a case of this one.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint dated after 26 January 2024 that either (a) proves in ZFC that a class K of models of a countable first-order theory omitting countably many types with a model of cardinality ℵ_{ω1} must have a model of cardinality continuum, or (b) proves the consistency of ZFC + such a K having a model of cardinality ℵ_{ω1} but no model of cardinality continuum (a genuine independence/refutation result), or (c) an update to Shelah's own problem lists or the Shelah archive marking this specific sub-case as resolved.
